newsitem.title: POLAND: POLISH BANKERS WANT TO CHANGE C.BANK CHARTER BILL.
newsitem.headline: POLISH BANKERS WANT TO CHANGE C.BANK CHARTER BILL.

text.p: The Polish Banking Association (ZBP) will propose to the Senate to ammend a newly passed bill so that part of banks' obligatory reserve requirement could be kept in longer-term treasury bonds, the ZBP said on Friday.
Currently banks have to keep 20 percent of zloty call deposits, 11 percent of term zloty deposits and five percent of all currency deposits in the central bank free of interest.
The ZBP wants the first nine percent of banks' reserve requirements to be kept with the central bank with no interest, and any the remaining part to be invested in Polish T-bonds.
"We will ask the Senate to take into consideration our proposal," Krzysztof Pietraszkiewicz told a news conferece.
A new bill on the central bank charter, which was passed by the lower house on Friday and sent to the Senate, envisions keeping all the reserves with the central bank interest-free.
